profile.entities: Yatra Online Limited; THCL (Holding); Subsidiaries (under NCLT merger)
profile.subseg: Corporate Travel (B2E); MICE; Domestic Hotels; Air Ticketing; API Distribution
profile.themes: Geopolitical disruption (West Asia) deferring MICE; Domestic tourism pivot; AI-driven expense management upsell; Corporate client diversification away from IT

bull_bear.body: Net cash position INR 2,230mn; Strong operating cash flow INR 761mn (FY26) vs INR 73mn (FY25); Holding company (THCL) sold 1.8% stake to fund legal restructuring (NCLT merger of subsidiaries), no further dilution expected.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical conflicts impacting international travel/MICE; Airfare volatility compressing margins; Agentic AI shifting consumer demand channels (mitigated by B2E focus); Regulatory changes in aviation/tourism.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Resilient and confident; Acknowledges Q4 geopolitical 'blip' as temporary; Emphasizes structural diversification away from IT sector; Highlights strong Q1 recovery signals.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: IT services exposure reduced from 20% (FY24) to <7-10% of total B2E, de-risking the AI-disruption narrative for corporate travel; B2C segment is profitable and cash-generative, not a loss-leader, providing supplier leverage for B2B; MICE international transactions carry 3x-3.5x value vs domestic, explaining disproportionate Q4 revenue impact.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet is in a net cash position on the deck's own metric: Net Debt to Equity Ratio of (0.47)x in FY24, (0.17)x in FY25 and (0.18)x in FY26, versus 0.30x in FY23.
- Net Worth rose from INR 1,695 Mn (FY23) to INR 8,302 Mn (FY26), the step-up coming in FY24 alongside INR 4,663 Mn of financing-activity inflow and listing expenses of INR 54 Mn.
- Returns remain modest against that enlarged equity base: ROE 4.5% / (0.6)% / 4.7% / 5.6% and ROCE 22.3% / 4.3% / 4.3% / 5.8% for FY23 to FY26.
- Working capital absorbed cash heavily in FY23 and FY24 (deployment of INR 1,898 Mn and 1,453 Mn) before turning positive — cash flow from operations moved from INR (1,424) Mn in FY24 to INR 761 Mn in FY26.
- Borrowings are small: non-current borrowings of INR 12 Mn and current borrowings of INR 704 Mn at FY26; no dividend or buyback is mentioned anywhere in the deck.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Air: Passenger vol +9.6% (Q4), +2% (FY26); Margin expanded to ~4% (FY26). Hotels: Room nights +36% (Q4), +16% (FY26); Margin ~9.25%. MICE: Disrupted in Q4 by West Asia conflict; shifting to domestic/SE Asia. B2C: ~30% of gross bookings, profitable (mid-high single digit margin).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| West Asia conflict deferred high-value international MICE and group travel bookings, causing Q4 revenue/EBITDA miss | Indian Hotels Company Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Management explicitly noted shift in customer preference from international to domestic programs; Yatra's domestic hotel supply growth aligns with broader domestic tourism push. |
| Rising airfares and geopolitical tension increased input costs for travel aggregators while fixed selling prices compressed margins | Yatra Online Limited | loser | High | Directly impacted Q4 EBITDA (-46% YoY) and PAT; though deferred business expected to return in FY27. |
| Potential long-term erosion of B2C traffic due to Agentic AI and direct airline channels | Sabre Corporation | beneficiary | Low | While Yatra claims resilience via B2E, any structural shift away from OTA websites towards GDS/Enterprise SaaS for complex bookings could favor backend providers over consumer-facing aggregators if B2C volumes stagnate. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "Yatra is India's largest managed corporate travel services provider, catering to over 1,300 large & medium corporates and over 60,000 SME clients, with an addressable employee base of more than 9 Mn", and separately "India's leading B2B Corporate platform by total spend and number of customers".
- "It is also one of India's largest OTA platforms and serves as a one-stop shop for leisure travel needs, with 80% of total traffic driven by direct and organic channels."
- Corporate stickiness is the stated lever: "Market leader in large corporate travel management segment", "High retention rates driven by deep tech integration" and "Best in class corporate travel management platform".
- "Industry Leading Supply of Domestic Hotels" — described as "Supplier of choice for other players in the industry (within and outside India)", i.e. Yatra also wholesales its hotel supply.
- Established in 2006; management team brings "over 90 years of cumulative industry experience".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] The FY25 cash flow shows "Acquisition of business" of INR (1,290) Mn, with Goodwill rising from INR 691 Mn (FY24) to INR 1,415 Mn (FY25) and unchanged in FY26; the deck does not name the acquired business.
- [Regulation] "One Time Statutory Impact of new Labour Codes" of INR 38 Mn was booked in FY26, described as "the one-time effect of change in Labour code".
- [Shareholding] As on 30 June 2026: Promoters 62.66%, FII 4.95%, DII 11.29%, Public 21.10%; CMP INR 112.45, Market Cap INR 17,645.23 Mn, 156.92 Mn shares outstanding, face value INR 1.00.
- [Airline incentives] Profitability was hit by "Lower airline-related income as regional airlines delayed finalization of their incentives for the current fiscal year given the uncertain business environment", with the deck saying "Commercial discussions are ongoing... we expect a positive outcome in most of these cases in Q2".
- [Authorship] The presentation was "prepared by Valorem Advisors", an independent investor relations firm, rather than solely in-house.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Air margin improved structurally from 2.7% (FY24) to 4% (FY26); Hotel margin 7.7% to 9.25%. Cost pressure: People cost up due to salary inflation and share-based payments in Q4; Discounting ratio optimized to ~48% of gross take (from 61% historically) driven by B2E mix.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Medium-term CAGR: 20% Revenue-less-Service-Cost, 30% Adjusted EBITDA; Q1 FY27 run-rates trending ~20% above Q4 FY26; Expect H2 FY27 to be materially stronger than H1 due to pent-up demand release.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Corporate pipeline robust: 55 new clients added in Q4 (INR 2,709mn annual billable potential) vs 40 in Q3; Full year 163 new clients (INR 9,568mn); Retention rate ~97%.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Mid-market corporate segment (new dedicated sales team); AI-driven expense management (Recap) upsell to 1,300+ enterprise base; API-led distribution scaling with affiliates; Domestic tourism infrastructure boom.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: FY26 marked record profitability with 27% revenue growth and 37.5% EBITDA expansion, proving resilience despite Q4 headwinds from West Asia conflict which deferred high-value MICE bookings. The strategic pivot away from IT-services dependency (now <10% of B2E) and successful upsell of AI-based expense management tools strengthen the long-term structural thesis, even as Q4 PAT fell 46% YoY due to temporary geopolitical shocks.

meta.thesis: FY26 marked record profitability with 27% revenue growth and 37.5% EBITDA expansion, proving resilience despite Q4 headwinds from West Asia conflict which deferred high-value MICE bookings. The strategic pivot away from IT-services dependency (now <10% of B2E) and successful upsell of AI-based expense management tools strengthen the long-term structural thesis, even as Q4 PAT fell 46% YoY due to temporary geopolitical shocks.
